Maya H: quick thread 11 need outbound for customers impacted by Dedicated pool provisioning delays this morning. draft below.

Maya H: ```Subject: Status update: Dedicated capacity provisioning delay affecting some new enterprise tenants

Hi <CustomerContact>,

Status: Resolved 1 Provisioning for Dedicated pools is restored.

What happened: between 08:05 and 10:22 UTC today an autoscaler regression caused new Dedicated pool assignments to queue instead of being allocated. This primarily affected recently ordered Dedicated seats and first-time tenant migrations resulting in delayed activation windows.

Impact: affected customers may have seen "Provisioning in progress" for longer than expected or received timeout errors when attempting to connect to a newly provisioned Dedicated endpoint. Existing Dedicated capacity and running workloads were not impacted.

What we did: engineering deployed a rollback to the autoscaler, manually reconciled queued allocations, and kicked off a targeted backfill to ensure all pending pools completed provisioning. Normal provisioning resumed at 10:22 UTC; all known pending pools were completed by 11:10 UTC.

If you were affected: your account team will post a provisioning completion timestamp in the tenant activity feed. If your activation timeline was disrupted and you
need a hands-on assist, reply to this email with the tenant ID and preferred 2-hour window and we
will prioritize a manual validation session.

Compensation: for tenants whose scheduled activation was delayed more than 4 hours, we will apply a one-time account credit equal to 3% of the first-month Dedicated commit (or up to $2,500 for smaller accounts). Enterprise renewals: we will coordinate account-level remediation with your renewal manager.

Preventing recurrence: we
have added a pre-deploy autoscaler e2e test that simulates allocation pressure and an ops guardrail to reject autoscaler changes without an explicit failover plan.

Resources: status.redwood.ai (incident #2026-DED-PRV), provisioning dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dedicated/provisioning, onboarding office hours today 16:00 UTC.

We
apologize for the disruption and appreciate your patience while we fixed this.




























































































Best,
CS Ops
```

Diego R: timeline numbers look right, but engineering confirmed manual reconciliation finished at 11:08 UTC not 11:10. change to 11:08. Also change the credit wording to "eligible for" instead of definitive language until Legal signs off.

Lina P: add a short checklist for CS teams to triage impacted renewals: tenant ID, original activation ETA, current status, renewal window flag. Also include migration owner contact.

Ben K: +1 on renewal checklist. Suggest we limit the $2,500 cap to accounts below $50k commit to avoid unusual cases.

Maya H: updated draft below with Diego/Lina/Ben edits. Legal please review compensation phrasing.

Maya H: ```Updated excerpt:
What we did: engineering rolled back the autoscaler change, reconciled queued allocations, and kicked off a targeted backfill; normal provisioning resumed at 10:22 UTC and queued pools completed by 11:08 UTC.

Compensation: affected tenants may be eligible for a one-time account credit equal to 3% of the first-month Dedicated commit (accounts with < $50k commit will receive up to $2,500). Enterprise customers will receive tailored remediation through their account teams. (Legal review pending.)

CS triage checklist: tenant ID, original activation ETA, provisioning completion timestamp, renewal window (yes/no), migration owner.
```

LegalBot: please avoid words like "will receive" for credits. Recommend: "may be eligible" and add an exceptions sentence: "Credits are subject to eligibility verification and applicable terms." Approve incident number format.

Diego R: engineering also requests adding note: "For customers with scheduled automated migration jobs, we recommend pausing automated retries until assigned pool shows status=Ready to avoid duplicate runs."

Maya H: added the pause recommendation. Can we finalize and schedule at 12:30 UTC?

Lina P: one minor language suggestion: replace "apologize" with "we're sorry" to match CS voice.

Ben K: +1. I'll prep renewal-impact summary template.

LegalBot: phrasing approved with suggested qualifiers.

Maya H: final draft below. scheduling outbound for 12:30 UTC. OpsBot can you queue?
